title: Thermostat schedule
body: Since October 15 the thermostat holds 21 °C by day and drops to 17 °C overnight. The night window from 23:00 to 6:00 saved about 700 rubles in November.

title: Washer drain filter
body: I clean the drain pump filter every three months, last time on March 12. After the cleaning the spin-cycle noise and the drum smell both went away.

title: Dishwasher salt
body: I keep a two-pack reserve of salt and top it up when hardness goes above 2 mmol/L. The panel indicator goes out after the first wash with a full fill.

title: Fridge temperature
body: I set 4 °C in the fridge section and minus 18 °C in the freezer using a thermometer, not the dial marks. Monthly checks showed milk keeps two days longer now.

title: Freezer inventory
body: I keep a freezer list on a magnetic board: after the February 3 audit we threw away zero food in a month instead of two bags before. The rule is simple: new items go to the back, old ones to the door.

title: Spice drawer
body: I moved spices into identical 100 ml jars with labels on top of the lids. Finding a jar went from half a minute to a couple of seconds, and the January audit cleared out everything expired.

title: Knife sharpening
body: I sharpen on a 1000/3000 stone every six weeks, holding a 15-degree angle on Japanese blades. Since switching from a honing rod to the stone, touch-ups are needed half as often.

title: Cutting boards
body: Boards are split by color: red for meat, green for vegetables, white for bread. Once a month I oil them with mineral oil, and they have stayed crack-free for a year.

title: Cast iron care
body: I heat the pan with a spoonful of oil after every wash and never use soap. The polymerized layer has held since April, and rust has not come back.

title: Tea storage
body: Tea lives in double-lid tin jars away from the stove. Aromatic sorts stopped fading: an oolong now lasts a full three months instead of six weeks.

title: Honey crystallization
body: Buckwheat honey sets within three weeks, which is normal, not spoilage. I liquefy it in a water bath no hotter than 40 °C to keep the aroma.

title: Freezing bread
body: I cut the loaf in half on purchase day and freeze the second half right away. Toasted, the thawed half is indistinguishable from fresh even on day three.

title: Robot vacuum map
body: I split the apartment into five zones on the robot's map and set a no-go on the office during calls. Scheduled cleaning at 10:00 on weekdays stopped tangling in cables after the second firmware update.

title: Windowsill herbs
body: Basil and green onion live in water glasses on the windowsill and move to soil after two weeks. A 12-hour grow light in winter keeps the harvest going year-round.

title: Seedlings on the window
body: I sow tomatoes on March 20 in covered trays and pot them up at the two-true-leaves stage. Lighting from 6:00 to 20:00 eliminated leggy stems completely.

title: Rose pruning
body: I prune roses to a live bud at a 45-degree angle in late April. Secateurs are wiped with alcohol between bushes, and black spot has not returned for two seasons.

title: Lawn aeration
body: I forked the lawn every 15 cm in May and top-dressed with sand. Puddles stopped forming after rain, and the bare patches filled in within six weeks.

title: Rain barrel
body: I put a 200-liter barrel under the downspout with a mesh guard against debris and mosquitoes. The July greenhouse watering ran on rainwater only, and the water bill dropped by a third.

title: Grill cleaning
body: I burn the grill on max for 15 minutes after each cook and brush the grate while hot. The deep strip-down with grease measurement happens once a season, in August.

title: Firewood stack
body: Logs are stacked bark-up with a hand-width air gap between rows. August wood burns without cracking: moisture ends up at 18 percent versus 30 for fresh-cut.

title: Chimney sweep
body: I call the sweep once a year before the season starts, in September. After cleaning the draft improves so much that lighting a fire takes five minutes instead of fifteen.

title: Attic ladder
body: I oiled the folding ladder hinges with silicone grease and tightened four hatch screws. The squeak is gone and the hatch closes into the catch without a slam.

title: Gutter cleaning
body: Gutters get cleaned twice a year: after leaf fall in November and after flowering in May. Since fitting baskets over the outlets, blockages have not repeated in two seasons.

title: Fence painting
body: I paint the fence in two coats a day apart, using paint with wax. The refresh lasts three years, while the neighbors' basic emulsion peels in a single season.

title: Squeaky door hinges
body: I inject lithium grease into the hinges with a syringe and take the door off for a full pin lubrication. The squeak stayed away for a year; I repeat it each shoulder season.

title: Water heater flush
body: I drain and flush the heater once a year in May; last flush yielded half a cup of scale. Heat-up time for the 80-liter tank is back to 40 minutes.

title: Faucet aerator
body: Every three months I unscrew the aerator and rinse the mesh from lime flakes. Pressure returned to normal, and water use for dishwashing fell by about a tenth.

title: Toilet flapper
body: I replaced the rubber flapper when a quiet constant trickle appeared. The next month's water bill dropped by 1.2 cubic meters.

title: Tub caulk
body: I cut away the old sealant and applied a sanitary compound with an anti-mold additive, exhaust fan off. The joint has stayed clean for 14 months.

title: Humidifier care
body: I rinse the humidifier tank weekly and fill it with filtered water only. No scale builds on the membrane, and the cartridge needs replacing every three months.

title: Fan lubrication
body: I put two drops of machine oil into each bearing of the floor fan before the season. The hum on medium speed disappeared and the blades spin up more quietly.

title: Iron soleplate
body: I run a damp cloth with a drop of vinegar over the soleplate at medium heat to lift scorch marks. Steam vents get a cotton swab every two months.

title: Sewing machine oil
body: I oil the bobbin case after every 20 hours of sewing. Skipped stitches stopped and the mechanism runs smoother.

title: Winter tires
body: I switch to winter tires when the daily mean drops to plus seven and run them at 2.3 bar. Braking distance on packed snow shortened noticeably, measured on an empty lot.

title: Engine oil change
body: I change the oil every 8 thousand kilometers instead of the 15 written in the old service book. Top-ups between changes dropped to zero.

title: EV charging
body: I keep the battery in the 20 to 80 percent corridor and charge at night on the cheap tariff. Full 100 percent charges happen only before a long trip.

title: Passport renewal
body: I filed the passport renewal online on May 12 and it was ready on May 27. Picked it up at the same office where I handed in the old one, no appointment needed.

title: Tax deduction folder
body: I keep a dedicated folder for deduction papers: certificates, contracts and payment slips go in on the day they arrive. Last year's return came together in one evening.

title: Insurance checkup
body: Every March I review the policies: coverage, deductible and the insured property list. The review caught an overlap between two policies and cut the premium by 15 percent.

title: Warranty registry
body: I keep a warranty spreadsheet: item, purchase date, term, receipt location. The faucet was replaced under warranty five days before it ended — without the sheet I would have missed it.

title: Receipt box
body: Paper receipts go into monthly envelopes, and photos of important ones go straight into the store's app. The kettle return went through on photos in ten minutes.

title: Budget envelopes
body: The monthly limit is split into four envelopes: food, transport, household, reserve. The quarter saw one overrun, when an annual subscription charged against the food envelope.

title: Utility meter readings
body: I submit water and electricity readings on the 25th of each month and keep meter photos in one album. The disputed July bill closed based on the photos within days.

title: Daily 15-minute sketch
body: I draw one small sketch a day after breakfast, timer set for 15 minutes. A quarter added up to 80 sheets, and my hand stopped fearing the blank page.

title: Watercolor supplies
body: I moved to pan watercolors and 300 gsm cotton paper. The paper switch mattered more than the paint switch: washes stopped coming out blotchy.

title: Clay and firing
body: Pieces dry under foil for a week, otherwise the teapot spout cracks. Firing at the community studio costs 400 rubles per load, and I go once a month.

title: Embroidery hoop tension
body: I prefer plastic hoops with a screw: the fabric does not shift on long stitches. My wrist stopped going numb after switching to a floor stand.

title: Bird feeder
body: The feeder hangs at one meter sixty and two meters from the bush, so the tits have somewhere to retreat. I refill it every three days with raw, unsalted seeds.
